items.statement: Cross-Curricular
Digital Citizen
items.notes: As responsible digital citizens, learners exhibit safe, ethical and informed use of technology in a Christ-like manner. Learners develop good technological habits while avoiding unnecessary traps. Learners have the opportunity to develop a wide range of skills, literacies, and abilities that extend beyond the classroom. Learners:

items.statement: Exercise responsible Christ-like behavior when using technology.
Demonstrate respect for diversity as Jesus modeled.
Practice safe, legal, and ethical use of information and technology.
Cultivate and manage their digital identity and reputation recognizing the permanence of the digital footprint.
Develop strategies to appropriately handle cyber-bullying.
Understand and comply with legal responsibilities in regard to copyright when using and sharing intellectual property.
Practice self-control and time-management.
Protect personal data to maintain digital privacy and personal security.
Enabled Learner
items.notes: Learners leverage technology to take ownership of their learning and develop academically, socially and spiritually. This may be facilitated through critical thinking, data analysis, agency, goal-setting, and problem solving. Learners:

items.statement: Employ appropriate technology in service to the church and community.
Use technology as a tool to engage in creative, productive, life-long learning.
Understand the primary functions of technology and be able to transfer those skills to explore new technologies.
Seek feedback from peers, teachers, experts and online tools to critique and improve their work.
Set personal learning goals using various technological methods and demonstrate understanding in a variety of ways.
Evaluate the validity, viewpoint and relevance of information gathered.
Dissect information into separate parts, extract vital data, develop models to problem solve and test prototypes.
Purposeful Communicator
items.notes: Learners articulate ideas and questions in clear and creative ways by using tools appropriate for the desired outcome, while maintaining a Christ-like approach. All communications reflect ethical and focused messages. Learners:

items.statement: Select effective platforms and tools for reaching preferred goals from a Christian perspective.
Share complex ideas with clarity and purpose.
Communicate logically using appropriate language.
Publish or present material that tailors the information and medium for desired audiences.
Use a variety of media and formats within digital environments to communicate ideas with authentic audiences and engage in faith-based activities.
Establish meaningful networks with peers and others.
Utilize technology to support reflective listening.
Global Collaborator
items.notes: Learners utilize technology to broaden and enrich their learning experiences through meaningful collaboration with peers and world community. Collaboration is a reflection of the way people solve problems, and technology tools help learners connect with others. Learners develop skills to navigate global challenges by examining issues and problems through multiple viewpoints. While using technology, learners:

items.statement: Engage a global audience to share the Gospel.
Establish meaningful connections with a broader community to strengthen and expand their learning experiences.
Communicate complex ideas effectively to diverse audiences.
Develop a greater understanding of how human organizations and actions impact global systems.
Articulate their own values in a cross-cultural setting.
Collaborate to work with others to investigate solutions.
Creative Developer
items.notes: While using a variety of technologies, learners become innovative designers creating unique, relevant and/or imaginative solutions. Encouraging creativity is pivotal in sharing Christian perspectives through productions. Learners:

items.statement: Create original media productions.
Produce, edit and responsibly remix digital resources.
Understand terminology, basic structure and process of coding.
Use algorithmic thinking to develop and evaluate automated solutions.
Identify and implement a targeted design process for developing concepts, testing theories and solving authentic problems.
Recognize design as part of a cyclical process that includes development, testing and refinement.
Appreciate ambiguity, perseverance and the ability to troubleshoot open-ended problems.
